Set the discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = 0$ for tangency and solve for $k$.
walkthrough:
Equate the curve and tangent equations to form an intersection equation:
$$(2k - 3)x^2 - kx - (k - 2) = 3x - 4$$

Rearrange into standard quadratic form $Ax^2 + Bx + C = 0$:
$$(2k - 3)x^2 - (k + 3)x - (k - 6) = 0$$

Set the discriminant $\Delta = B^2 - 4AC = 0$ for a single point of contact:
$$(-(k + 3))^2 - 4(2k - 3)(-(k - 6)) = 0$$
$$(k^2 + 6k + 9) + 4(2k^2 - 15k + 18) = 0$$
$$k^2 + 6k + 9 + 8k^2 - 60k + 72 = 0 \implies 9k^2 - 54k + 81 = 0$$

Divide by $9$ and solve the perfect square quadratic equation:
$$k^2 - 6k + 9 = 0 \implies (k - 3)^2 = 0 \implies k = 3$$

ai_rubric.Tangents to a Quadratic Curve: Equates curve and line (M1). Forms $(2k - 3)x^2 - (k + 3)x - (k - 6) = 0$ (DM1). Applies discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = 0$ (DM1). Simplifies to $9k^2 - 54k + 81 = 0$ (M1) and solves to get $k = 3$ (A1).
